caption:
Mountain biking in Costa Rica is rarely about the speed on the flats. It is about the patience required to earn the ridgeline. When the gradient tilts upward and the mud demands everything from your lungs, the gear on your handlebars becomes secondary to the silence of the forest around you. There are no crowds here, no engines, and no schedules to keep—only the rhythm of your own breathing against the vast, green slope of the Talamanca massif. You eventually reach the top, not because you were fast, but because you were steady enough to stay with the mountain until it let you pass.
